findings.body: The mutation throws FORBIDDEN ("you_do_not_have_permission") even though the variable and intent are "admin or owner", so team admins cannot add guests; only owners can.
findings.failure_mode: Authorized team admins are incorrectly rejected at runtime.
findings.impact: The mutation throws FORBIDDEN ("you_do_not_have_permission") even though the variable and intent are "admin or owner", so team admins cannot add guests; only owners can.
findings.root_cause: Boolean operator mismatch: conjunction used for a check whose semantics (and name) are disjunctive.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the `&&` between the `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` checks to `||` (or just use `isTeamAdmin`, which already returns truthy for ADMIN and OWNER).
findings.title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of either
findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee calls viewer.bookings.addGuests for a team event booking.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 46-48 show `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Repository context confirms isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER roles (L264-283), so using && requires both calls to succeed, meaning only OWNERs pass. The variable name and intent clearly indicate disjunction, but conjunction is used.

raw_findings.body: The mutation throws FORBIDDEN ("you_do_not_have_permission") even though the variable and intent are "admin or owner", so team admins cannot add guests; only owners can.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorized team admins are incorrectly rejected at runtime.
raw_findings.impact: The mutation throws FORBIDDEN ("you_do_not_have_permission") even though the variable and intent are "admin or owner", so team admins cannot add guests; only owners can.
raw_findings.root_cause: Boolean operator mismatch: conjunction used for a check whose semantics (and name) are disjunctive.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the `&&` between the `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` checks to `||` (or just use `isTeamAdmin`, which already returns truthy for ADMIN and OWNER).
raw_findings.title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of either
raw_findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee calls viewer.bookings.addGuests for a team event booking.

raw_findings.body: The blacklist filter does not match, so the blocked address is persisted as an attendee and receives booking emails, defeating the blocklist that other call sites (handleNewBooking, checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked) enforce case-insensitively.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Security control silently bypassed for mixed-case input.
raw_findings.impact: The blacklist filter does not match, so the blocked address is persisted as an attendee and receives booking emails, defeating the blocklist that other call sites (handleNewBooking, checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked) enforce case-insensitively.
raw_findings.root_cause: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest value is compared without normalization.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the guest email before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (ideally using extractBaseEmail like handleNewBooking).
raw_findings.title: Blacklisted guest emails bypassed by non-lowercase input
raw_findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains "blocked@example.com" and the client submits guest "Blocked@Example.com".

raw_findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees, so `createMany` inserts two attendee rows for the same address and the guest receives duplicate emails; the uniqueness rule enforced only client-side in AddGuestsDialog is not enforced server-side.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate attendee records and duplicate notification emails created from a valid API call.
raw_findings.impact: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees, so `createMany` inserts two attendee rows for the same address and the guest receives duplicate emails; the uniqueness rule enforced only client-side in AddGuestsDialog is not enforced server-side.
raw_findings.root_cause: Server-side validation omits the duplicate-email constraint that the UI schema enforces.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a uniqueness refinement to the schema (e.g. `.refine((g) => new Set(g.map((e) => e.toLowerCase())).size === g.length)`) or dedupe `guests` in the handler before filtering.
raw_findings.title: addGuests input schema allows duplicate guest emails
raw_findings.trigger: Any client (or a direct tRPC call bypassing the dialog) sends `guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]`.

raw_findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` stays true because the component stays mounted, so the reopened dialog shows the stale "Emails must be unique and valid" error with an empty form.

raw_findings.body: `message` is always a non-empty template string (at minimum "undefined: "), so the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never render and users can see "undefined: " prefixed toasts; the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` locale key is dead.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Fallback branch and its i18n key are unreachable; malformed toast text.
raw_findings.impact: `message` is always a non-empty template string (at minimum "undefined: "), so the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never render and users can see "undefined: " prefixed toasts; the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` locale key is dead.
raw_findings.root_cause: Template literal is used as the truthiness guard for the fallback, which is never falsy.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Build the message conditionally, e.g. `const message = err.data?.code ? `${err.data.code}: ${t(err.message)}` : t("unable_to_add_guests");` and pass it directly to showToast.
raw_findings.title: Unreachable toast fallback makes unable_to_add_guests key dead
raw_findings.trigger: Any mutation error, including one with no `err.data?.code` and empty message.

validated_findings.body: The mutation throws FORBIDDEN ("you_do_not_have_permission") even though the variable and intent are "admin or owner", so team admins cannot add guests; only owners can.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Authorized team admins are incorrectly rejected at runtime.
validated_findings.impact: The mutation throws FORBIDDEN ("you_do_not_have_permission") even though the variable and intent are "admin or owner", so team admins cannot add guests; only owners can.
validated_findings.root_cause: Boolean operator mismatch: conjunction used for a check whose semantics (and name) are disjunctive.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change the `&&` between the `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` checks to `||` (or just use `isTeamAdmin`, which already returns truthy for ADMIN and OWNER).
validated_findings.title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of either
validated_findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee calls viewer.bookings.addGuests for a team event booking.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 46-48 show `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Repository context confirms isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER roles (L264-283), so using && requires both calls to succeed, meaning only OWNERs pass. The variable name and intent clearly indicate disjunction, but conjunction is used.

validated_findings.body: The blacklist filter does not match, so the blocked address is persisted as an attendee and receives booking emails, defeating the blocklist that other call sites (handleNewBooking, checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked) enforce case-insensitively.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Security control silently bypassed for mixed-case input.
validated_findings.impact: The blacklist filter does not match, so the blocked address is persisted as an attendee and receives booking emails, defeating the blocklist that other call sites (handleNewBooking, checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked) enforce case-insensitively.
validated_findings.root_cause: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest value is compared without normalization.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the guest email before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (ideally using extractBaseEmail like handleNewBooking).
validated_findings.title: Blacklisted guest emails bypassed by non-lowercase input
validated_findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains "blocked@example.com" and the client submits guest "Blocked@Example.com".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 77 shows `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased (line 71) but guest is not normalized. Repository context shows handleNewBooking uses `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()` for case-insensitive comparison, confirming inconsistency.

validated_findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees, so `createMany` inserts two attendee rows for the same address and the guest receives duplicate emails; the uniqueness rule enforced only client-side in AddGuestsDialog is not enforced server-side.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate attendee records and duplicate notification emails created from a valid API call.
validated_findings.impact: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees, so `createMany` inserts two attendee rows for the same address and the guest receives duplicate emails; the uniqueness rule enforced only client-side in AddGuestsDialog is not enforced server-side.
validated_findings.root_cause: Server-side validation omits the duplicate-email constraint that the UI schema enforces.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a uniqueness refinement to the schema (e.g. `.refine((g) => new Set(g.map((e) => e.toLowerCase())).size === g.length)`) or dedupe `guests` in the handler before filtering.
validated_findings.title: addGuests input schema allows duplicate guest emails
validated_findings.trigger: Any client (or a direct tRPC call bypassing the dialog) sends `guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 5 shows server schema `z.array(z.string().email())` without uniqueness refinement. The handler's uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees, not duplicates within the input array. Client schema has uniqueness check but server does not enforce it.

validated_findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable metadata

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Move the schema to module scope with a distinct name (e.g. `guestEmailsSchema`) outside the component body.
validated_findings.title: Validation schema rebuilt on every render inside the dialog component
validated_findings.trigger: Every render of AddGuestsDialog (each keystroke in MultiEmail) re-executes the zod builder.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Schema recreation per render is a minor performance concern, not a functional bug. The naming shadow is a style issue. Category is 'style' and impact is negligible performance overhead.
